description: Bento, the office suite that fits in a file

summary.one_liner: Bento is an open-source PowerPoint alternative that packages a full slide editor, viewer, and presenter into a single self-updating HTML file.
summary.what_it_does: Bento is a presentation app delivered as one HTML file of about 560 KB, with no account or installer needed. Opening the file in a modern browser gives you the editor, and saving rewrites the file with the deck embedded inside. The deck data is stored as plain JSON in a readable block near the top of the file. Presentations use Morph transitions, where elements sharing an id animate between slides, and Reveal.js handles navigation. The app includes built-in charts (bar, line, pie, scatter), speaker view, comments, layouts, PDF export, and 8 UI languages. Collaboration uses end-to-end encrypted sync with a CRDT, and an optional offline mode blocks outside network traffic. The README also describes an AI-friendly workflow where agents or chatbots can edit the JSON directly.
use_cases: build a slide deck without Microsoft Office
send a presentation that opens in any browser
edit slides offline with local AI models
collaborate on slides with encrypted sharing
let an AI agent generate or revise a presentation
how_to_run: Open bento.page/slides in a browser to try it without installing
Download Bento_Slides.bento.html from the GitHub Releases page and open it in a browser
npm run dev (starts the dev server)
notable: Entire app is a single self-saving HTML file with the deck embedded as plaintext JSON
Morph transitions animate elements that share an id between slides
In-house dependency-free chart engine and CRDT for collaboration
E2EE collaboration where keys live in the file itself; optional blind sync relay in server/sync-worker/
Signed self-updates that write a new file, keeping the old one as rollback
caveats: Editing is desktop-first; phones are described as good for viewing and presenting only
Undo during live collaboration is snapshot-based and can revert a collaborator's concurrent edit to the same property
Presence names are claims rather than verified identities; enterprise identity signing is designed but not built
Only the slides app is shipped; notes, sheets, and vault apps are roadmap items
